text.text: The WonderSwan Color was released in Japan in 2000 as the successor to Bandai's original WonderSwan handheld. It added a color display while maintaining compatibility with existing software. The system featured a low-cost design, long battery life, and a library that included role-playing games, puzzle games, and licensed titles such as Final Fantasy. Developed with input from former Nintendo engineer Gunpei Yokoi, the WonderSwan family competed primarily against Nintendo's Game Boy line in Japan.
